newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria banks to raise monthly rates on deposits.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria banks to raise monthly rates on deposits.

text.p: Bulgaria's commercial banks will raise interest rates on monthly deposits to 20-22 percent from five to six percent in line with a new record high main rate of 300 percent annually, a bank official said.

"The Association of Commercial Banks decided that its members will increase rates on monthly lev deposits to 20-22 percent following the hike of the central rate," the association's co-chairman Ognian Enchev told reporters.
The new monthly interest rates will go into effect from Monday, September 30, Enchev said. @
Monthly interest rate on deposits ranged between five and six percent under the previous central interest rate (CIR) of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) of 108 percent.
On Monday the BNB raised the CIR to an annual 300 percent or 25 percent monthly, in force from Tuesday, in another bid to boost confidence in the slumping national currency, the lev.
"Commercial banks however could follow BNB's main rate no longer than a couple of months," Enchev said. @
The BNB's governor Lyubomir Filipov told a news conference earlier on Tuesday that the new CIR might be considered as a temporary measure. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
